correctness.rationale: The exact floor-difference identity yields s*g=g+epsilon-u with g(n)=2n-1. Formal decomposition by powers of 2 gives G(t)=(H+tJ)/((1-2t)(1-t)), where H(1)=1 and J(1)=0. Since J^{*j}(m)=0 when j>Omega(m), the coefficient of t^a in S(t) vanishes for a>Omega(m)+2. At a=Omega(m)+2 only 2E*t^2 contributes; its coefficient is the stated strictly positive multinomial. The empty odd-part case is explicit. The original defining recurrence was cross-checked against the divisor recurrence through 512, and 563 sharp boundaries and 624 zero tails through 16384 were checked from an actual companion script. Finite computations are corroboration, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: This is an infinite sharp support and exact boundary theorem for a recently defined quadratic arithmetic recurrence: for every fixed odd m, all sufficiently deep dyadic extensions vanish, with threshold determined exactly by the multiplicity-weighted number of odd prime factors. The final nonzero coefficient is an explicit positive multinomial product. It explains a new structural zero phenomenon not implied merely by the established prime-value and first composite examples; it is not a finite enumeration or arbitrary numerical gain.
